outcomeNote: Aggadic exposition extending the mishna's 'not part of society'

segments.en: Similarly, «bar Kappara taught: An angry person»

segments.he: לֹא עָלְתָה בְּיָדוֹ אֶלָּא רַגְזָנוּתָא. וּלְאָדָם טוֹב מַטְעִימִים אוֹתוֹ מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו. וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ לֹא בַּמִּקְרָא וְלֹא בַּמִּשְׁנָה וְלֹא בְּדֶרֶךְ אֶרֶץ – דּוֹר הֲנָאָה מִמֶּנּוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְמוֹשַׁב לֵצִים לֹא יָשָׁב״ – מוֹשָׁבוֹ מוֹשַׁב לֵצִים.
segments.en: «has managed» to acquire «only anger [ragzanuta],» i.e., nothing beneficial comes through anger; in the end he is left with nothing but the anger itself. «And a good person is given the fruit of his actions to taste. And» with regard to «any» person «who does not engage in» the study of «Bible, nor» the study of «Mishna, nor» the «desired mode of behavior,» one should «vow to not» derive «benefit from him,» and one should have no contact with him, «as it is stated: “Nor sat in the seat of the scornful”» (Psalms 1:1). The «seat» of this person is certainly the «seat of the scornful,» as he is engaged in nothing but idle matters.

moves.summary: An angry person gains nothing but anger

moves.cueHe: ולאדם טוב מטעימים אותו מפרי מעשיו
moves.summary: A good person is given the fruit of his deeds

moves.cueHe: וכל שאינו לא במקרא ולא במשנה ולא בדרך ארץ – דור הנאה ממנו
moves.summary: Vow not to benefit from one lacking all three
His seat is the seat of the scornful

edges.about: one engaged in neither Bible, Mishna nor derekh eretz sits in the seat of the scornful

positions.claim: an angry person gains only anger; a good person tastes the fruit of his deeds; one should vow no benefit from one lacking Bible, Mishna and derekh eretz
